chains.title: Speculative ESR1-mediated effect on PELI2
chains.element: Unannotated regulatory sequence at or near the variant (unverified)

links.claim: The testable hypothesis is that ESR1 binds T more strongly than C, but this direction is unsupported: no QBiC-SELEX result or variant-overlapping ChIP-seq peak is reported. ESR1 expression makes it a plausible candidate in MCF7, not evidence of occupancy at this base.
This chain requires an unannotated regulatory sequence because no cCRE overlaps the variant; the evidence does not establish that such an element functions here.
PELI2 is only a candidate target because it is the nearest listed protein-coding gene; no supplied evidence links it to regulation by this variant.
MCF7 is a proposed context because ESR1 is highly expressed there, but no TF peak over the variant was found in this biosample.

The proposed downstream effect is increased breast-cancer risk if greater ESR1 binding increases PELI2 expression; neither this regulatory direction nor a link to risk is established by the supplied evidence.

predictions: Relative to H0, allele-specific ESR1 assays will show greater binding to T than C.
Under this chain's unverified activating-element assumption, T will increase PELI2 expression; disrupting ESR1 or editing T back to C will reduce that effect.
falsified_if: A sensitive allele-specific assay finds no greater ESR1 binding to T than C.
Variant editing or ESR1 perturbation does not produce the predicted linked change in PELI2 expression.

chains.title: Very weak alternative: FOXA1-mediated effect on PELI2
chains.element: Unannotated regulatory sequence at or near the variant (unverified)

links.claim: The testable hypothesis is that FOXA1 binds C more strongly than T, but the direction is unsupported: no QBiC-SELEX result or variant-overlapping ChIP-seq peak is reported, and the supplied evidence does not establish FOXA1 occupancy or expression in MCF7.
This chain requires an unannotated regulatory sequence because no cCRE overlaps the variant; the evidence does not establish that such an element functions here.
PELI2 is only a candidate target based on proximity; no supplied evidence connects it to this variant.
MCF7 is a proposed context, but the supplied evidence shows no TF peak over the variant there and gives no FOXA1 expression evidence for this line.
The proposed downstream effect is reduced breast-cancer risk if greater FOXA1 binding represses PELI2; neither this regulatory direction nor a link to risk is established by the supplied evidence.

predictions: Relative to H0, allele-specific FOXA1 assays will show greater binding to C than T.
Under this chain's unverified repressive-element assumption, C will reduce PELI2 expression; disrupting FOXA1 or editing C to T will remove that effect.
falsified_if: A sensitive allele-specific assay finds no greater FOXA1 binding to C than T.
Variant editing or FOXA1 perturbation does not produce the predicted linked change in PELI2 expression.

checks.why: Could find directly relevant reported allele-specific binding or functional assays that are absent from the supplied evidence.
Would test whether ESR1 is expressed in the proposed context; expression would not establish variant occupancy but could inform TF plausibility.
Would assess whether PELI2 has evidence connecting it to breast cancer, while not by itself establishing it as the variant's target.

matrix.test: Allele-specific EMSA using C and T probes with MCF7 nuclear extract and an ESR1-specific supershift or depletion control.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible ESR1-dependent binding difference between the C and T probes.
Greater ESR1-dependent binding to the T probe than the C probe.
No predicted ESR1-specific T-over-C difference; this chain instead predicts greater FOXA1 binding to C.

matrix.test: Isogenic C-to-T editing in MCF7 cells followed by ESR1 and FOXA1 occupancy assays and PELI2 expression measurement.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible variant-dependent occupancy or PELI2 expression change.
T increases ESR1 occupancy and, under the proposed activating-element assumption, PELI2 expression.
C increases FOXA1 occupancy and, under the proposed repressive-element assumption, reduces PELI2 expression.

next_experiment: The cheapest test separating the top two hypotheses (H0 and H1) is the allele-specific ESR1 EMSA with an ESR1-specific supershift or depletion control. It directly tests H1's proposed T-over-C binding difference; a positive result would motivate, but would not by itself establish, the proposed element-to-PELI2-to-disease chain.
